name: VAG DQ250 / 02E DSG mechatronic (J743, PQ platforms)
cpu: PowerPC, big-endian (observed in real reads); later 02E software on an Infineon TriCore

read_methods.notes: Bench over CAN on the 20-pin T20e plug (ecupinouts lists a K-line variant on pin 1; MaxxECU marks pin 1 K-line as unused). The PowerPC-generation software is handled as a 0x68000-byte (416 KiB) image (12 code sectors + one 32 KiB CAL sector); the TriCore-generation 02E300013N reads seen are 0xB0000 bytes with a 64 KiB CAL first. Reading the CAL over OBD and the OBD programming protocol are not documented in the cited sources; flash containers for 02E are VAG FRF/ODX files (method 0x11 table cipher + compression per vag-tcu-tools), not decoded by OpenTune for 02E yet.

notes: Six-speed wet-clutch DSG (02E) with the mechatronic/TCU (J743) inside the gearbox. Two software generations were seen in real reads: PowerPC (big-endian; ecudef temic-dq250-02e, checksum dq250-02e = CRC-16/MCRF4XX sector table, real-image-tested on six reads) and a later Infineon TriCore build (02E300013N; ecudef temic-dq250-02e-tricore, checksum not located). The DQ250-MQB JAMCRC (checksum id dq250) does NOT apply to 02E. The 02E927770xx numbers are mechatronic (hardware) part numbers; 02E300xxx numbers are the software/gearbox part numbers found in the flash image. Vehicle list and 02E927770 part numbers from MaxxECU's DQ250 integration notes (not exhaustive). Protocols left empty: not stated by the sources.

pins.note: MaxxECU: present but not used; ecupinouts: K-line on a second hardware variant.

bench.notes: +12 V to 11 and 13, ground 19, CAN-H 10 / CAN-L 15 (both sources). MaxxECU additionally wires 18 (+12 V) and 16 (ground).
bench.resistor_notes: Put a 120 ohm resistor across CAN-H/CAN-L if your interface does not terminate (ecupinouts). Run CAN as a twisted pair.

safety_note: Bench safety: use a current-limited bench supply (12-13.8 V, start with a low current limit) and a fuse in the +12 V lead; connect ground first. Confirm every pin with a multimeter on YOUR unit before applying power - ground pins should show continuity to each other (and usually the housing), and hardware revisions can differ from the sources. A CAN bus needs about 60 ohm between CAN-H and CAN-L (two 120 ohm terminations): add a 120 ohm resistor if neither the unit nor your interface terminates. Swapped CAN-H/CAN-L just gives timeouts; +12 V on a signal pin can destroy the unit.

sources.title: MaxxECU: VAG DSG (DQ250) wiring and hardware requirements
OpenTune docs/DSG.md: 02E layout and checksum analysis of real reads
dspl1236/vag-tcu-tools docs/PLATFORM_RESEARCH.md (MIT): FRF method 0x11 for DQ200/DQ250/DL382

obd.protocol: KWP2000 over VW TP2.0 to logical address 0x02 on the powertrain CAN (what OpenTune's read-only opentune dsg uses; not yet confirmed on a car)
obd.notes: Neither a complete read nor programming over OBD is documented in the cited sources. Factory software for 02E comes as VAG FRF/ODX containers (method 0x11, vag-tcu-tools); the programming session and its security access are not documented.

bench.how: CAN on the 20-pin T20e plug: +12 V to 11 and 13, ground 19, CAN-H 10, CAN-L 15 (both sources agree); 120 ohm across CAN-H/CAN-L if the interface does not terminate. It speaks the same diagnostic protocol as in the car; what can be read that way is not documented.

boot.notes: No cited public source documents a boot or bootstrap mode for the 02E unit (PowerPC or TriCore software). The open DQ250-MQB bench path (SBOOT) belongs to the 0D9 unit, not to this one.

security.notes: Not documented in the cited sources; opentune dsg sends no security-access service. OpenTune ships no OEM key.
